subject.title: fix(opencode): public models work without configured credentials

question: Should OpenClaw officially support OpenCode Zen’s upstream credentialless `public`-key mode for zero-input-cost models, and accept `modelId` as part of the provider synthetic-auth context needed to implement it?
rationale: OpenCode’s client source and the branch proof support the mechanics, but the mode changes OpenClaw’s provider-auth behavior while public Zen documentation reportedly still requires a key; choosing the durable product and plugin-SDK contract needs owner intent.

options.title: Approve the scoped public-model contract
options.body: Accept the upstream client contract for zero-input-cost OpenCode Zen catalog models, keep paid and unknown models credential-gated, and land with user-facing provider documentation.

options.title: Keep OpenClaw credential-gated
options.body: Decline credentialless Zen execution until the provider publishes a matching user-facing contract, leaving the current authentication behavior unchanged.

options.title: Request a narrower SDK direction
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want model-scoped synthetic auth to use a different plugin-SDK seam before enabling any provider.

recommendation.title: Approve the scoped public-model contract
recommendation.body: Accept the upstream client contract for zero-input-cost OpenCode Zen catalog models, keep paid and unknown models credential-gated, and land with user-facing provider documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository policy identifies provider and plugin-SDK compatibility choices as owner-reviewed; no more specific current-main history owner was established in the supplied evidence.
